2026 SEMA Show • Honda Racing Releases Its First-Ever In-House Made Parts for the Civic Type R and Integra Type S
Nissan Returns to the Annual SEMA Show Featuring a 300-HP Sentra Spec-V Revival Concept, Two Z Cars
45 photos
Photo: Nissan
The 2026 SEMA Show continues the tradition of the annual automotive trade show held at the Las Vegas Convention Center in Nevada, and Nissan eagerly joins the party, once again, with a triple concept showcase.
Actually, this trio might only be the appetizer for the Japanese automaker’s North American subsidiary, as the 2026 SEMA Show is still around the corner and the brands might showcase only a few of their stars in advance. So far, we have already seen at least some of the reveals and hints from Dodge, Ford, Toyota, or Mitsubishi, each showcasing their strengths.
Mitsubishi, for example, revealed the 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition ; Toyota has already shown a wacky quintet of SUVs and trucks on snow tracks along with the Crown Signia GT-S Performance Concept; Dodge wants to celebrate 90 years of Mopar with a special package for the Charger fastback coupe, and the Blue Oval is focusing on the Bronco, as far as we can tell.
Now Nissan joins the preview party with a revival of the Sentra Spec-V and two enthusiast-inspired Z concepts, “each offering a fresh take on Nissan performance and the possibilities of personalization.” There will be something for every sports car enthusiast: Z heritage, modern motorsports, as well as the tuner scene.
Nissan has a reserved booth in the Central Hall at the Las Vegas Convention Center, from November 3 through 6, and the headliner is, for sure, the Nissan Sentra Spec-V Concept which revisits the spirit of a beloved sport compact car – the Sentra SE-R arrived in North America 35 years ago and the new concept is “a tribute to the community that made the Sentra SE-R a star of the import car scene.”
While it still appears like a regular Nissan Sentra, the sport compact sedan is now choke full of Nismo parts, featuring a 300-hp build of its 2.0-liter engine thanks to turbocharging, mixed with an upgraded six-speed manual transmission from the Nissan Juke Nismo RS. There are also GT‑R-sourced Brembo brakes, bespoke Nismo coilovers and anti-roll bars, GT‑R-sourced Recaro front seats, and some rad Nismo LM-RS1 alloy wheels to round out the performance enhancements with the 19-inchers.
There’s also a fully custom body kit along with a GT-R Nismo rear spoiler to complete the look, and the car rides on 265/35R19 Yokohama Advan Neova AD09 tires! The first of the two Zs is the Nissan Project NAT2 SCCA Touring 2 sports car, developed in-house by the Nissan Acceleration Team (NAT), an all-volunteer group of employees who play with motorsports in their free time. As the name implies, it was created to comply with SCCA Touring 2 specifications featuring upgrades for the engine, suspension, and braking systems using both Nismo and aftermarket parts.
Last but not least is also a Datsun S30 Concept - Formula Drift champion and Z enthusiast Chris Forsberg, a longtime Nissan collaborator, spins the original Z toward the restomod area with the S30 concept fitting a twin-turbo V6 powertrain from the current Z. There are also Nismo upgrades added to the engine, several major body panels were replaced with lightweight carbon fiber, and there are also unique suspension and braking components.
There’s also a Nissan Z FS6 six-speed manual transmission, a Nismo R200 limited-slip differential, and Garrett PMAX turbochargers; a Nismo 40th decal set mixed with a stunning Nissan Seiran Blue paint; a ton of Techno Toy Tuning components for the suspension, Nismo forged wheels, Wilwood brakes, and a very nice interior featuring OMP Silverstone racing seats and many other things.
